anomalies.observed: The netlist shows all VDD pins of FCC2 (STM32H753) and NAVC2 (STM32F405) on unconnected nets, not on any 3.3V rail.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the 3.3 V LDO produces 3V3 for MCUs and sensors; all MCU VDD pins must be connected to the 3.3V rail.

evidence.quote: 3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors) ... produces 3V3 for "MCUs and Sensors"

anomalies.impact: Both microcontrollers receive no power, so the board cannot boot or function at all.

anomalies.observed: FCC2 VCAP pins 48 and 73 are connected to UART3_FCC2 pins 3 and 4 on nets NET0082 and NET0116, with no decoupling capacitors to ground.
anomalies.expected: VCAP pins are internal regulator outputs requiring 2.2uF decoupling capacitors to GND; the UART3 connector should carry UART TX/RX signals, not VCAP.

evidence.quote: programming/debug via SWD, USB DFU, and UART-to-USB

anomalies.impact: The STM32H7 internal regulator is not properly decoupled and is exposed on a connector, likely preventing the MCU from running and making the UART3 interface nonfunctional.

anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW U6 pin 1 (A0) is tied to +3.3V, which sets the I2C address to 0x41.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the PCA9685PW I2C address is 0x40, which requires A0 to be tied to GND.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The PWM driver responds at 0x41 instead of 0x40, so servo control will fail unless the firmware is changed to use the wrong address.
